title: NuoDB
text:
SQL compliant, NuoDB's database technology is classified as "NewSQL".[1,2] It has a distributed object architecture that works in the cloud,[1,3] which means that when a new server is added in order to scale-out the database, the database runs faster.[4,5,6,7] The database scales out without sharding. The database distributes tasks amongst several processors to avoid bottlenecks of data.[8] It uses peer-to-peer messaging to route tasks to nodes,[9] and it is ACID compliant.[10]

The database uses a "tiered approach — comprising multiple, redundant tiers of transaction engines (TE) and storage managers (SM)." This approach helps scale the data predictably in the cloud. NuoDB domains consist of several redundant TEs and SMs that can run on the same platform. Adding database capacity can be done by adding more TEs or SMs.[11] The NuoDB 2.6 release added support for active-active database deployments across multiple Amazon Web Services (AWS) availability zones.[12] Unlike other database systems, NuoDB makes it possible to expand its databases by adding more servers rather than simply replacing hardware.[13]

The system was designed to align with – and expand upon – IBM computer scientist Edgar F. Codd's 12 rules for relational databases.[14] It adds the ability to run anywhere; elastic scalability; nonstop availability; a single, logical database; and distributed security.[15] It is available in a free developer version ("Community Edition") and an enterprise version.[5,16,17] The Community Edition was expanded on January 31, 2017 to enable scale-out across multiple hosts.[18]

With the release of version 3.0 (2017), NuoDB expanded its ecosystem beyond Amazon Web Services, adding Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Red Hat environments and expanded multi-availability zone deployment for hybrid or multi-cloud environments.[19] NuoDB Operator achieved Red Hat OpenShift Operator Certification in 2019.[20,21] Support for Kubernetes Operators, public clouds (Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure), and cloud-native and cloud-agnostic capabilities was introduced in version 4.0 (2019), along with a new feature for assessing database health and performance.[22,23]
